prompt: Compute the average of two ints twice: once with integer division (truncated) and once as an exact double. Complete both methods to see how casting changes the result.
explanation: When both operands of / are ints, Java performs integer division and simply drops the fractional part, truncating toward zero -- so 7 / 2 is 3 and -7 / 2 is -3. To keep the fraction, at least one operand must be a double: dividing by 2.0 (or casting with (double)(a + b)) promotes the whole expression to double arithmetic. The two methods run the same math but differ only in the type of the division.
hints: For the truncated version, (a + b) / 2 with all ints already drops the fraction for you.
For the exact version, if both operands are ints the fraction is lost BEFORE the return happens.
Divide by 2.0 instead of 2, or cast the sum: (double)(a + b) / 2.
